expat_boomer_retiree.profession_past: corporate executive, small business owner, civil servant/teacher
expat_boomer_retiree.primary_goal: Secure a long-stay retirement visa (KITAS Lansia/Silver Hair/Second Home) and settle legally in Bali with healthcare access and property tenure clarity.
pain_points: KITAS Lansia age/income thresholds keep changing and agents give conflicting answers
Cannot own freehold land — confused between Hak Pakai, leasehold 25+25, and nominee schemes (which they've been warned are illegal)
Health insurance after 65 is expensive or refused — unclear if BPJS covers them as KITAS holders
Tax residency trap: 183-day rule, worldwide income, NPWP obligations vs. home-country pension taxation
Visa agent horror stories — overpaid, got wrong visa, or agent disappeared with passport
Currency risk on pension (AUD/GBP/EUR vs IDR) and difficulty opening local bank account without KITAS
Loneliness and scam exposure — widowed or solo retirees targeted by younger partners or fake investment schemes
Repatriation of remains / inheritance for Indonesian-situated assets if spouse dies
content_preferences: testimonials from other retirees by name and age
hook_patterns_that_work: story (other retiree's journey, named, with photo)
comparison (Bali vs Portugal vs Malaysia MM2H)
verbatim_quotes: I'm 67, my wife is 63, we've sold the house in Perth and we want to do this properly — no nominee, no shortcuts. Can you walk us through KITAS Lansia start to finish?
My agent in Seminyak quoted me 35 million rupiah for the retirement visa but my neighbour paid 22 million last year. How do I know what's fair and what's legitimate?
We've been coming to Ubud for 15 years on tourist visas and B211s. Now Immigration is tightening up and we're scared of being blacklisted. Is it too late to regularise?
If I buy a villa on leasehold for 25 years, I'll be 92 when it expires. What happens to my wife if I die first — does the lease transfer?
I don't trust the Facebook groups anymore, too many opinions. I want to sit down with someone qualified, see their license, and get it in writing.
trust_signals: physical office in Kerobokan/Sanur with signage
named lawyer or notaris (PPAT) with credentials shown
Google Reviews 4.7+ with 200+ reviews mentioning retirees by name
written fixed-price quote on letterhead with tax invoice (faktur pajak)
referral from another retiree in their expat circle
press mentions in Jakarta Post, Bali Discovery, The Bali Sun
years in business (10+) and AHU/Kemenkumham registration number visible
staff who speak clear English and respond within 24h by email

expat_techie_pma.geo_origin: EU (DE/NL/FR/IT) + North America + AU/NZ, secondary UK + Singapore
expat_techie_pma.profession_past: SaaS founder/CTO, senior software engineer, digital product consultant
expat_techie_pma.primary_goal: Set up a compliant PT PMA in Bali to legally run my remote tech business, get a KITAS, and optimize tax residency without triggering CFC rules back home.
pain_points: Conflicting info on minimum capital (IDR 10B paid-up vs. committed) and whether KBLI 62xxx actually allows my SaaS/consulting activity
Notary and agent quotes ranging 3x for the same PMA+KITAS package with no clear scope breakdown
Fear of accidental PE (permanent establishment) exposure in home country while being tax resident in ID
Opening a corporate BCA/Mandiri account as a fresh PMA — KYC loops, deposit requirements, rejected without local director
LKPM quarterly reporting, BPJS, and annual tax filings in Bahasa that no one warned them about at signup
Visa agent disappears after KITAS issuance — no lifecycle support for amendments, NIB/OSS updates, share transfers
Unclear if they can legally invoice international clients from the PMA without VAT/PPN traps
content_preferences: long-form breakdown posts with actual IDR numbers
side-by-side comparison tables (PT PMA vs KITAS investor vs E33G)
founder case studies with real timelines and costs
short explainer reels under 90s with on-screen captions
structured PDFs/checklists for OSS-RBA, LKPM, BPJS
AMA threads and Loom walkthroughs over polished ads
hook_patterns_that_work: specific-number hook (e.g. 'PT PMA in 47 days, IDR 38.5M all-in')
myth-bust question ('Do you really need 10 billion rupiah in the bank?')
checklist teaser ('7 things your agent won't tell you about LKPM')
verbatim_quotes: I don't need motivation, I need the actual KBLI code that lets my SaaS invoice Stripe from a PT PMA without PPN headaches.
Three agents, three prices, three different stories about the 10 billion — who's actually reading the BKPM reg here?
I'll pay premium, I just want one firm that stays with me past KITAS pickup and handles LKPM every quarter without me chasing them on WhatsApp.
My CPA back home is freaking out about CFC and PE — can you give me something in writing I can send her?
Can we do the whole thing remotely before I land, or do I really have to fly in for the notary?
trust_signals: founder referrals in private Slack/Telegram communities
named lawyer or notary with SIUP + PERADI number visible
transparent fixed-fee scope with what's NOT included listed
Google Reviews with recent PMA-specific cases (not just visa runs)
LinkedIn presence of the actual consultants, not just the brand
published case studies with IDR figures and timelines
written engagement letter in English + Bahasa
press mentions in Tech in Asia / KrAsia / Bali Post
direct access to a named account manager on WhatsApp

id_founder_pma.geo_origin: Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya, Bali (Indonesian nationals returning from overseas study/work)
id_founder_pma.primary_goal: Strutturare la mia startup come PT PMA per ricevere investimento estero, ottenere credibilità internazionale e proteggere la struttura legale per scaling regionale ASEAN
pain_points: Confusione tra PT lokal vs PT PMA: quando conviene davvero il PMA per founder indonesiano (capitale minimo 10B IDR, KBLI restrictions, nominee risks)
Tax structure complessa: PPh badan 22%, dividend WHT 20% per shareholder estero, transfer pricing scrutiny dal DJP
BKPM/OSS-RBA bureaucracy: NIB, izin usaha, LKPM reporting trimestrale, sanzioni se ritardi
Capital injection requirements: paid-up capital tracking, escrow, modal disetor minimo 25% del modal dasar
Cap table dilution con investor stranieri (VC Singapore/HK) e governance dual-class shares non riconosciuta in UU PT
Compliance multilayer: BPJS Kesehatan + Ketenagakerjaan, WLKP, RPTKA per expat hires, audit obligation se omzet >50M IDR
Exit strategy unclear: M&A vs IPO IDX vs holding Singapore — dove parcheggiare IP e cap table
content_preferences: case study founder Indonesia (DealStreetAsia, Tech in Asia)
podcast lungo formato (Endgame, Thirty Days of Lunch)
decision_journey_stages: awareness via peer founder e VC associate
research desk su regolamenti BKPM e benchmark fee studi legali
consideration con 2-3 consulenti shortlist (big4 vs boutique vs Bali Zero)
decision dopo intro call + proposal dettagliata + referenze founder esistenti
post-decision: retention su compliance ricorrente (LKPM, tax, payroll)
hook_patterns_that_work: numero specifico (es. '10B IDR minimum capital — qui come strutturarlo')
peer comparison ('cosa fanno i founder serie A')
